questions.question: In an election between 2 candidates, 5% of the votes were invalid. The winning candidate got 2200 votes and the losing candidate got 1600 votes. The losing candidate got what percentage of the total votes cast ?
questions.solution:
Let the total votes cast be $V$. Since $5\%$ of the votes cast were invalid, the valid votes are $95\%$ of $V$. The two candidates received all the valid votes, so:
Valid votes = $2200 + 1600 = 3800$.
Thus, $0.95V = 3800 \implies V = \frac{3800}{0.95} = 4000$.
The percentage of the total votes cast that the losing candidate got is:
$\frac{1600}{4000} \times 100 = 40\%$.

questions.question: In a constituency, 85% of the total number of people on the electoral roll cast their votes during an election. 10% of the votes cast were declared invalid. If there were 3,00,000 people on the electoral roll, and Dharam secured 1,37,700 valid votes, what percentage of the total number of valid votes did Dharam secure?
questions.solution:
Total people on the electoral roll = $300,000$.
Votes cast = $85\%$ of $300,000 = 255,000$.
Since $10\%$ of the votes cast were invalid, valid votes = $90\%$ of $255,000 = 229,500$.
Dharam secured $1,37,700$ valid votes.
Percentage of the total valid votes Dharam secured = $\frac{1,37,700}{229,500} \times 100 = 60.0\%$.

questions.question: In an election between two candidates, 20% of the registered voters did not cast their vote and 40 votes were declared invalid. The winner got 42% of the registered votes and was declared the winner by 112 votes. What was the number of registered voters ?
questions.solution:
Let the total number of registered voters be $x$.
Votes cast = $80\%$ of $x = 0.80x$.
Valid votes = $0.80x - 40$.
Winner's votes = $42\%$ of $x = 0.42x$.
Losing candidate's votes = Valid votes - Winner's votes = $(0.80x - 40) - 0.42x = 0.38x - 40$.
The winner won by $112$ votes, so:
$0.42x - (0.38x - 40) = 112 \implies 0.04x + 40 = 112 \implies 0.04x = 72 \implies x = 1800$.

questions.question: In an election between two candidates, 10% of the voters did not cast their votes and 75 votes were found invalid. The winner got 50% of the total votes expected and won by 170 votes. How many voters were enrolled in the voters’ list?
questions.solution:
Let the total number of voters enrolled in the list be $x$.
Votes cast = $90\%$ of $x = 0.90x$.
Valid votes = $0.90x - 75$.
Winner's votes = $50\%$ of total expected votes $x = 0.50x$.
Losing candidate's votes = Valid votes - Winner's votes = $(0.90x - 75) - 0.50x = 0.40x - 75$.
Winner won by $170$ votes, so:
$0.50x - (0.40x - 75) = 170 \implies 0.10x + 75 = 170 \implies 0.10x = 95 \implies x = 950$.

questions.question: In an election, the winner was supported by 46% of all the voters in the list, and he got 410 votes more than his only rival. 10% of the voters on the voters’ list did not cast their votes, and 60 voters cast their ballot papers blank. How many voters were on the list ?
questions.solution:
Let the total number of voters in the list be $x$.
Winner's votes = $46\%$ of $x = 0.46x$.
Since $10\%$ of voters did not cast their votes and $60$ cast blank ballots, the valid votes cast for candidates = $0.90x - 60$.
Only rival's votes = $(0.90x - 60) - 0.46x = 0.44x - 60$.
Winner won by $410$ votes, so:
$0.46x - (0.44x - 60) = 410 \implies 0.02x + 60 = 410 \implies 0.02x = 350 \implies x = 17500$.

questions.question: In an election, 12% of the voters in the voter list did not cast their votes, whereas 84 voters cast their ballot papers blank. There were only two candidates: Ramagya and Shravan. The winner, Ramagya, was supported by 54% of all the voters in the list. He got 1456 more votes than his rival, Shravan. Find the total number of voters in the list.
questions.solution:
Let the total number of voters in the list be $x$.
Valid votes = $x - 0.12x - 84 = 0.88x - 84$.
Ramagya's votes = $54\%$ of $x = 0.54x$.
Shravan's votes = Valid votes - Ramagya's votes = $(0.88x - 84) - 0.54x = 0.34x - 84$.
Ramagya got $1456$ more votes, so:
$0.54x - (0.34x - 84) = 1456 \implies 0.20x + 84 = 1456 \implies 0.20x = 1372 \implies x = 6860$.

questions.question: In an election, 95% of the total voters cast their votes. In this election, there were only two candidates A and B. The winner A, by obtaining 75% of the total votes, defeated his contestant B by 5500 votes. Find the total number of voters in the election.
questions.solution:
Let the total number of voters in the election be $x$.
Votes cast = $95\%$ of $x = 0.95x$.
Winner A got $75\%$ of total votes = $0.75x$.
Since there are only two candidates, candidate B got: $0.95x - 0.75x = 0.20x$.
Winner A defeated B by $5500$ votes, so:
$0.75x - 0.20x = 5500 \implies 0.55x = 5500 \implies x = 10,000$.

questions.question: Two candidates contested an election. The winning candidate got 52% of the valid votes and won by a margin of 360 votes. If 10% of votes were declared invalid then what was the total number of votes polled?
questions.solution:
Let the total votes polled be $V$.
Valid votes = $90\%$ of $V = 0.90V$.
Winner got $52\%$ of valid votes, so loser got $48\%$ of valid votes.
Winner won by a margin of $52\% - 48\% = 4\%$ of valid votes.
$0.04 \times 0.90V = 360 \implies 0.036V = 360 \implies V = 10,000$.

questions.question: In a state election between two parties, 83% of the voters cast their votes, out of which 4% of the votes were declared invalid. Party A got 156611 votes which were 83% of the total valid votes. Find the total number of votes enrolled in that election. (Consider integer part only)
questions.solution:
Let the total number of enrolled voters be $x$.
Votes cast = $0.83x$.
Valid votes = $96\%$ of votes cast = $0.96 \times 0.83x$.
Party A's votes = $83\%$ of valid votes = $0.83 \times 0.96 \times 0.83x = 156611$.
$0.661344x = 156611 \implies x = \frac{156611}{0.661344} \approx 236807$.

questions.question: In an election between two candidates, 15% of the voters in the town did not cast their votes, and 10% of votes polled were declared invalid. The winning candidate got 62% of the valid votes and won by a majority of 3,672 votes. How many valid votes did the losing candidate get ?
questions.solution:
Let the total valid votes be $V_v$.
Winning candidate got $62\%$ of valid votes, so losing candidate got $38\%$ of valid votes.
Winner's majority = $62\% - 38\% = 24\%$ of valid votes.
$0.24 \times V_v = 3672 \implies V_v = \frac{3672}{0.24} = 15300$.
Losing candidate's valid votes = $38\%$ of $15300 = 0.38 \times 15300 = 5814$.

questions.question: In an election between two candidates, the defeated candidate secured 42% of the valid votes polled and lost the election by 2545800 votes. If 365500 votes were declared invalid and 30% people did not cast their vote, what was the approximate number of people (in millions) in the electorate who did NOT cast their votes ?
questions.solution:
Let valid votes polled be $V_v$.
Defeated candidate got $42\%$ of $V_v$, so winner got $58\%$ of $V_v$.
Difference = $58\% - 42\% = 16\%$ of $V_v = 2545800$.
$0.16V_v = 2545800 \implies V_v = 15,911,250$.
Total votes polled = $V_v + 365,500 = 15,911,250 + 365,500 = 16,276,750$.
Since $30\%$ of electorate did not cast votes, total votes polled = $70\%$ of total electorate $E$.
$0.70E = 16,276,750 \implies E = 23,252,500$.
Number of people who did not vote = $30\%$ of $23,252,500 = 6,975,750 \approx 7\text{ million}$.

questions.question: In an election between two candidates, y% of the voters did not vote. 10% of the votes cast were declared invalid, while all the valid votes were cast in favour of either of the two candidates. The candidate who got 59.375% of the valid votes cast was declared elected by 2484 votes. If the number of people eligible to vote in that election was 16,000, what is the value of y ?
questions.solution:
Let valid votes cast be $V_v$.
Winner got $59.375\%$ of valid votes, so loser got $40.625\%$ of valid votes.
Winner won by a majority of $59.375\% - 40.625\% = 18.75\%$ of valid votes.
$0.1875 \times V_v = 2484 \implies V_v = \frac{2484}{0.1875} = 13248$.
Since total eligible voters = $16,000$:
Votes cast = $\frac{13248}{0.90} = 14720$ (since $10\%$ of votes cast were invalid).
Percentage of voters who voted = $\frac{14720}{16000} \times 100 = 92\%$.
Thus, $y = 100 - 92 = 8$.

questions.question: Three-seventh of voters promise to vote for A and the rest promise to vote for B. Of these, on the last day 12% of the voters went back on their promise to vote for A and 20% of voters went back on their promise to vote for B and A lost by 234 votes. The total number of voters was ?
questions.solution:
Let the total number of voters be $700x$.
Initially, A's share = $300x$, B's share = $400x$.
On the last day, $12\%$ of A's promised voters ($36x$) voted for B, and $20\%$ of B's promised voters ($80x$) voted for A.
Actual votes for A = $300x - 36x + 80x = 344x$.
Actual votes for B = $400x - 80x + 36x = 356x$.
A lost by $234$ votes:
$356x - 344x = 234 \implies 12x = 234 \implies x = 19.5$.
Total number of voters = $700 \times 19.5 = 13650$.

questions.question: In an election between A and B, every fifth vote polled was marked as invalid by the machine. In the remaining votes, A wins the election with a margin of 2500 votes or 10% of the total votes polled, over B. If 90% of the invalid votes would have been in favour of B, then which of the following would have been the result of the election ?
questions.solution:
Let total votes polled be $V$.
Invalid votes = $\frac{V}{5} = 0.20V$. Valid votes = $0.80V$.
Margin of victory = $10\%$ of $V = 2500$ votes $\implies V = 25000$.
Valid votes = $0.80 \times 25000 = 20000$.
Let A's and B's original votes be $a$ and $b$:
$a + b = 20000$ and $a - b = 2500 \implies a = 11250$, $b = 8750$.
Invalid votes = $5000$.
If $90\%$ of the invalid votes ($0.90 \times 5000 = 4500$) go to B:
B's new votes = $8750 + 4500 = 13250$.
A's votes = $11250$.
B wins by $13250 - 11250 = 2000$ votes.
As a percentage of total votes polled: $\frac{2000}{25000} \times 100 = 8\%$.

questions.question: In an election between P, R and S, 1/10 of the total votes polled are invalid. Votes polled in favour of R and S are half of the total votes polled, and they get equal votes. Due to a fault in the machine, half of the votes of S and half of the invalid votes are counted additionally in favour of R. What is the overall percentage of votes secured by R due to the fault ?
questions.solution:
Let the total votes polled be $100$.
Invalid votes = $10$.
Votes for R and S together = $50$. Since they get equal votes, originally R = $25$ and S = $25$.
Due to the fault, additional votes for R = $\frac{\text{votes of S}}{2} + \frac{\text{invalid votes}}{2} = 12.5 + 5 = 17.5$.
Total votes secured by R = $25 + 17.5 = 42.5$.
Percentage of votes secured by R = $42.5\%$.

questions.question: Hari, Kamal and Lalit contested an election in which 6050 votes were polled and none of the votes were invalid. Kamal got 42% more votes than the total votes obtained by Hari and Lalit together. If Lalit obtained only 8% of the total polled votes, find the number of votes obtained by Hari.
questions.solution:
Total votes = $6050$. Lalit's votes $L = 8\%$ of $6050 = 484$.
Let $H, K, L$ be the votes of Hari, Kamal, and Lalit.
$H + K + L = 6050$.
Given, $K = 1.42(H + L)$.
Substitute $K$ in the total sum:
$(H + L) + 1.42(H + L) = 6050 \implies 2.42(H + L) = 6050 \implies H + L = 2500$.
Since $L = 484$, $H = 2500 - 484 = 2016$.

questions.question: In an election, a voter has choices to vote for one candidate out of three candidates. There is also an option 'None Of The Above' (NOTA) to reject all candidates. The three candidates get votes that are 6 times NOTA. The winner gets votes that are twice the second runnerup's votes. The first runner-up gets 900 votes more than NOTA and defeats the second runner-up by 150 votes. What is the total number of votes polled ?
questions.solution:
Let NOTA votes be $x$.
Votes of candidates $W + F + S = 6x$.
Given: $W = 2S$, $F = x + 900$, and $F - S = 150 \implies S = x + 750$.
Then, $W = 2(x + 750) = 2x + 1500$.
Substitute these into $W + F + S = 6x$:
$(2x + 1500) + (x + 900) + (x + 750) = 6x \implies 4x + 3150 = 6x \implies 2x = 3150 \implies x = 1575$.
Total votes polled = $7x = 7 \times 1575 = 11025$.

questions.question: In an election, there were three candidates: A, B and C. 10% of the eligible voters did not vote. Out of those who voted, 45% voted for A, 35% voted for B and the remaining 20% voted for C. 30% of the votes polled for A and 20% of the votes polled for B were later deemed invalid, while all the votes polled for C were deemed valid. If A got 882 more valid votes than B did, how many valid votes did C receive ?
questions.solution:
Let the total votes polled be $100x$.
Votes for A = $45x$, B = $35x$, C = $20x$.
Valid votes for A = $70\%$ of $45x = 31.5x$.
Valid votes for B = $80\%$ of $35x = 28x$.
Difference in valid votes between A and B = $31.5x - 28x = 3.5x$.
Given $3.5x = 882 \implies x = 252$.
Valid votes received by C = $20x = 20 \times 252 = 5040$.

questions.question: A, B and C contested an election. All the votes polled were valid. A got 38% of the total votes. For every 45 votes polled, B got 18 votes. The winner got 5,760 more votes than the person who received the least number of votes. The total number of votes polled was:
questions.solution:
Let total votes polled be $T$.
Percentage of votes for A = $38\%$.
Percentage of votes for B = $\frac{18}{45} \times 100 = 40\%$.
Percentage of votes for C = $100\% - 38\% - 40\% = 22\%$.
The winner is B ($40\%$) and the person with least votes is C ($22\%$).
Difference = $40\% - 22\% = 18\%$.
$0.18T = 5760 \implies T = 32000$.

questions.question: Chamanlal, Arshad and Jagit Singh contested an election. All the votes polled were valid. Arshad got 35% of the total votes. For every 35 votes Chamanlal got 14 votes. The winner got 4950 more votes than the person who received the least number of votes. Find the total number of votes polled.
questions.solution:
Let total votes polled be $T$.
Arshad got $35\%$ of votes.
Chamanlal got $\frac{14}{35} \times 100 = 40\%$ of votes.
Jagit Singh got $100\% - 35\% - 40\% = 25\%$ of votes.
Winner (Chamanlal) got $4950$ more than Jagit Singh (least):
$40\% - 25\% = 15\% \implies 0.15T = 4950 \implies T = 33000$.

questions.question: In an election, there were four candidates and 95% of voters cast their votes. One candidate got 25% of the votes while the other three shared the remaining votes in the ratio of 6 : 7 : 2. The difference of votes secured by the candidate standing 3rd to the candidate standing 4th is equal to 69198. Find the votes secured by the winning candidate.
questions.solution:
Let the total votes cast be $V$.
Candidate 1 got $25\%$ of $V$.
Remaining votes = $75\%$ of $V$.
Other three candidates got votes in ratio $6 : 7 : 2$ of the remaining $75\%$:
Candidate 2 = $\frac{6}{15} \times 75\% = 30\%$ of $V$.
Candidate 3 = $\frac{7}{15} \times 75\% = 35\%$ of $V$.
Candidate 4 = $\frac{2}{15} \times 75\% = 10\%$ of $V$.
Ranking of candidates: 1st: $35\%$ (winner), 2nd: $30\%$, 3rd: $25\%$, 4th: $10\%$.
Difference between 3rd and 4th = $25\% - 10\% = 15\% = 69198$.
$0.15V = 69198 \implies V = 461320$.
Winning candidate's votes = $35\%$ of $461320 = 161462$.

questions.question: Three candidates P, Q and R contested an election. Out of the total votes on a voter list 20% did not vote and 25% of the polled votes were invalid. R got 3600 votes, which were 20% more than that of what Q got. If P got only 45% of the total votes, then find out the number of votes the winner got.
questions.solution:
Let the total votes in the voter list be $T$.
Polled votes = $80\%$ of $T$.
Valid votes = $75\%$ of polled votes = $0.75 \times 0.80T = 60\%$ of $T$.
Given, R got $3600$ votes, which is $20\%$ more than Q:
$R = 1.2Q \implies Q = 3000$.
P got $45\%$ of $T = 0.45T$.
Valid votes = $P + Q + R \implies 0.60T = 0.45T + 3000 + 3600 \implies 0.15T = 6600 \implies T = 44000$.
Votes obtained by candidates:
P = $0.45 \times 44000 = 19800$, Q = $3000$, R = $3600$.
Winner got $19800$ votes.

questions.question: In an election only two candidates contested. 70% of the voters casted their votes and 340 casted votes declared invalid. Winner got 784 valid votes more than his opponent, if the number of valid votes received by the winner 38% of the number of registered total voters, then find how many registered voters cast their votes?
questions.solution:
Let total registered voters be $T$.
Votes cast = $0.70T$.
Valid votes = $0.70T - 340$.
Winner's votes $W = 38\%$ of $T = 0.38T$.
Opponent's votes $L = W - 784 = 0.38T - 784$.
Since $W + L = \text{Valid votes}$:
$0.38T + 0.38T - 784 = 0.70T - 340 \implies 0.76T - 784 = 0.70T - 340 \implies 0.06T = 444 \implies T = 7400$.
Number of registered voters who cast their votes = $0.70 \times 7400 = 5180$.
